paraphrase: Case 1, Zhaozhou's dog: a monk asked whether a dog has buddha-nature; Zhaozhou said 'wu' (no). Wumen: to study Chan you must pass the barrier of the patriarchs, and this one word 'wu' is it. With your 360 bones and 84,000 pores rouse a mass of doubt and investigate 'wu' day and night; do not take it as nothingness or as the 'no' of being and non-being; it is like swallowing a red-hot iron ball you cannot spit out; all former wrong knowledge is swept away, inside and outside become one piece, like a mute who dreams and knows it only himself; suddenly it bursts open, shaking heaven and earth, and you are free on the brink of birth and death.

paraphrase: Case 19, the ordinary mind is the Way: Zhaozhou asked Nanquan 'what is the Way?' — 'the ordinary mind is the Way' — 'can one aim at it?' — 'to aim is to deviate' — 'without aiming, how know it is the Way?' — 'the Way is not a matter of knowing or not knowing; knowing is delusion, not knowing is blankness; truly reaching the Way beyond doubt, it is vast like space.' Wumen's verse: spring has its hundred flowers, autumn its moon … if nothing idle weighs on the mind, that is the best season.

paraphrase: Case 6, the World-Honoured One holds up a flower: on Vulture Peak the Buddha held up a flower; all were silent, only Mahākāśyapa smiled. The Buddha said: 'I have the treasury of the true Dharma eye, the wondrous mind of nirvāṇa, the true form without form, the subtle Dharma gate, not established on words and letters, a special transmission outside the teachings; I entrust it to Mahākāśyapa.' Wumen: if the eye can be transmitted, the Buddha deceived people; if not, why approve Kāśyapa alone?

paraphrase: Wumen's preface: the Buddha's words take mind as the source and the gateless as the Dharma gate; if it is gateless, how will you pass through? What enters by the gate is not the family treasure; what is gained through conditions begins and ends. He used the old cases as 'tiles to knock on the gate'; one who goes straight in with a single sword, careless of danger, cannot be stopped.

paraphrase: Wumen's Admonitions on Chan (appended): following rules and measures is binding oneself without a rope; roaming freely without restraint is heretics and Māra's army; keeping the mind clear and still is the heretical Chan of silent illumination; letting the mind go and forgetting conditions is falling into a deep pit; being alert and unobscured is wearing chains and a cangue; thinking of good and evil is heaven and hell; views of buddha and Dharma are two iron mountains; being aware of thoughts as they arise is toying with spirits; sitting blankly in samādhi is making a living in the ghost cave; neither advancing nor retreating is a dead man breathing.
